name: Caelum
introduction: is the Chisel, introduced by Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in the 1750s. It is one of the smallest and faintest constellations.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Lacaille named it after an engraver’s chisel. Caelum is so faint that only two of its stars are brighter than fifth magnitude, and it sits in an empty-looking region between Columba and Eridanus.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Alpha Caeli](hip:21770) is a white star 66 light-years away, and [Beta Caeli](hip:21861) a yellow-white star.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: RR Caeli is an eclipsing pair of a white dwarf and a red dwarf, with a giant planet orbiting both stars.
